chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him).

'If you see fit, O my Master, to teach me a supplication with which I may supplicate at the end of my prayers, by which Allah will gather for me the goodness of the world and the Hereafter.' So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'You should say.'

'I seek Refuge with Your Benevolent Face, and Your Might which cannot be assailed, and Your Power, from which nothing can be prevented, from the evil of the world and the Hereafter, and from the evil of all pains.'

key_terms.خَيْرَ الدُّنْيَا وَ الْآخِرَةِ: The goodness of the world and the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after daily prayers for protection and goodness?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration highlights the Imam's role in providing concise, potent supplications for daily spiritual practice, emphasizing reliance on Allah's attributes of majesty and omnipotence. The du'a serves as a comprehensive shield against worldly and otherworldly afflictions, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating divine protection into the post-prayer routine.
